sql: SELECT m.description, SUM(t.amount) AS total FROM main.transactions AS t JOIN main.mcc_codes AS m ON t.mcc = m.mcc GROUP BY m.description ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 10
why: One SELECT, approved tables and columns, an approved function, and a limit of 10. Nothing to fix.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM main.cards AS c WHERE c.has_chip = true
why: A single-number aggregate returns one row, so it needs no LIMIT.

sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.transaction_at) AS year, COUNT(*) AS n FROM main.transactions AS t GROUP BY year ORDER BY year LIMIT 20
why: EXTRACT is on the approved list, and GROUP BY year uses an alias the query itself defines.

sql: SELECT c.card_brand, AVG(c.credit_limit) AS avg_limit FROM main.cards AS c GROUP BY c.card_brand
why: Valid, but it returns many rows with no limit. The gate adds LIMIT 100 instead of rejecting it.

sql: SELECT t.mcc, COUNT(*) AS n FROM main.transactions AS t GROUP BY t.mcc
why: Same story: a missing bound can only be tightened, so LIMIT 100 is added.
cvv is not an approved column. Leaving off the table alias does not help: unaliased columns are checked too.
Only SELECT is allowed. This is a read-only assistant.
Wildcard projections could expose columns nobody approved.

sql: SELECT t.amount FROM source.transactions AS t LIMIT 5
why: Only the approved main schema may be queried, never the private source tables.

sql: SELECT t.mcc FROM main.transactions AS t LIMIT 5000
why: An explicit limit above 100 is refused. Only a missing limit gets fixed.

sql: SELECT t.mcc FROM main.transactions AS t LIMIT 1; DROP TABLE main.cards
why: Exactly one statement is allowed, so a second one smuggled after a semicolon is rejected.

sql: SELECT read_csv_auto('secrets.csv') AS x FROM main.cards AS c LIMIT 1
why: Only approved functions may be called, so reading a file from disk is refused.
